candidates.boundary: Read-only browser navigation: a CKB transaction hash and the consumer’s explicit network are converted to the provider’s documented /tx/<hash>?network=<network> route.
candidates.valueHypothesis: The consumer currently directs transaction hashes to a generic explorer page. A transaction-flow inspector could make inputs, outputs, fee and cell lineage easier to inspect; this is an inferred product benefit, not a requested feature.
candidates.adapter: Validate the 0x-prefixed 32-byte hash, preserve the consumer network (testnet), call the provider deep-link builder, and allow navigation only to the pinned HTTPS origin.

findings.explanation: The provider route parser requires a 0x-prefixed 32-byte CKB transaction hash. The consumer link is built from a value returned by its CCC signer submission call; runtime value validation remains required.
The consumer has a source-declared testnet configuration and the provider type contract permits testnet; this does not prove the transaction exists on that network.

The consumer already exposes an external transaction-view link and the provider accepts a transaction deep link. The proposed adapter changes navigation only; it does not share a wallet, signer or transaction builder.
Static source evidence does not establish that the provider deployment or its network RPC is currently available.
No transaction is signed, rebuilt, broadcast, or validated by the proposed link adapter.
A bounded prior-art check must run after candidate generation; a source-level URL contract does not establish that this pair is already integrated or used.

candidates.nextExperiment: Run the pinned provider URL builder and parser with a valid transaction hash on the consumer network, reject malformed hashes and unsupported networks, then open a real consumer-produced testnet transaction in the deployed read-only visualizer if a public transaction is available.

priorArt.scope: Eight anonymous GitHub Search API queries: issues and pull requests in each candidate repository, using the counterpart repository alias and bounded transaction-visualization/cell-lineage terms across indexed titles, bodies and comments. This does not establish that no prior proposal or integration exists.

persistence.reason: Persisted through the existing opportunity and evidence tables; no new lifecycle or adoption state was created.

limitations: Static source footprints do not prove runtime behavior or deployment availability.
The opportunity value is inferred from source interfaces, not an explicit consumer request.
The existing Pudge explorer link is a working alternative; the proposed provider may improve transaction-flow inspection but is not demonstrated as superior for every task.
Shared GitHub ownership is retained as a potential relationship-bias concern.
Prior-art search is bounded to indexed issue and pull-request title/body results; no absence guarantee is made.
